Title: API unit test suite crashes on a clean clone (no .env): service-context.test.ts exits via env.ts process.exit(1)
Environment: E1 local, macOS, Node 26.10, clean `npm ci`, no apps/api/.env
Repro steps:
1. Fresh clone, `npm ci`
2. `npm run build -w @canavo/shared`
3. `npm test` (no apps/api/.env)
Expected: All unit tests pass without secrets or a database — unit tests must be hermetic
Actual: `@canavo/api:test  FAIL src/services/service-context.test.ts — Error: process.exit unexpectedly called with "1" ❯ src/env.ts:43`; 13 tests never ran; turbo exits 1. CI passes only because it injects env vars.
Test ID: existing service-context.test.ts (13 tests) + `env -i … npx vitest run`
Notes: Fix: apps/api/vitest.config.ts supplies test-only dummy env vars only when unset. Root cause (module-level process.exit on import) revisited in Phase 3.

Title: `npm run lint` cannot run: apps/web has no ESLint config so `next lint` stops at an interactive setup prompt and exits 1
Repro steps:
1. `npm ci`
2. `npm run lint`
Expected: Lint runs non-interactively and reports findings
Actual: `? How would you like to configure ESLint?` prompt → `npm error Lifecycle script lint failed` (exit 1). Lint is not part of CI so this was never noticed.
Notes: Fix: apps/web/.eslintrc.json (next/core-web-vitals) + eslint@8.57.1, eslint-config-next@14.2.35. Now 0 errors, 3 warnings (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps). api/shared/mobile still have no lint → Phase 3 (strict config).

Title: Access token remains valid for up to 15 min after logout
Environment: E1 local, API dist build on :4100, seed data
Repro steps:
1. POST /auth/login as cashier@canavo.local → accessToken A, refreshToken F
2. POST /auth/logout {refreshToken: F} → 204
3. GET /auth/me with `Authorization: Bearer A`
Expected: 401 — a logged-out session can no longer be used (brief P8 'logout invalidation')
Actual: 200 with the user profile. Logout revokes only the refresh-token family; the stateless JWT stays valid until expiry (ACCESS_TTL 15 min). Same applies to a stolen token after the user logs out on a shared POS terminal.
Notes: Options: (a) bump tokenVersion on logout (logs out ALL devices of the user); (b) per-session id (sid) claim checked against the refresh family, revoked on logout (per-device); (c) accept risk + shorten TTL to 5 min. Recommend (b). Changes auth behaviour → asking before implementing.

Title: Build artifact apps/web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo is committed and rewritten by every build/typecheck (dirty tree after any build)
Repro steps:
1. Clean checkout
2. `npm run build`
3. `git status`
Expected: Working tree stays clean after a build
Actual: ` M apps/web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`
Notes: Fix: `git rm --cached`, `*.tsbuildinfo` added to .gitignore.

Title: Cross-tenant read: GET /attendance/calendar?userId= returns any user's attendance and leave (any business)
Repro steps:
1. Business B has a cashier with attendance + approved sick leave
2. Log in as manager@ (business A)
3. GET /attendance/calendar?month=2026-10&userId=<B cashier id>
Expected: 403/404, no data
Actual: 200 with B's attendance records (incl. notes) and leave reasons. StaffAttendance/LeaveRequest are not tenant-scoped and the handler only checked role. Also cross-outlet within a business.
Notes: Fix: target user resolved via tenant-scoped prisma.user and, below owner, an outlet the caller shares.

Title: ReDoS: menu bulk upload 'Sizes'/'Ingredients' cell parser is quadratic — one 5 MB upload blocks the API event loop for all tenants
Repro steps:
1. Upload a CSV whose Sizes cell is 'a' + 200,000 spaces + '='
2. Observe API stalls
Expected: Parsing is linear; request completes in ms
Actual: Regex /^(.*?)\s*[=:]\s*([^=:]+)$/ backtracks O(n²): 200k chars = 63 s of blocked event loop (64k = 6.8 s). 5 MB cap allows multi-hour stall.
Notes: Fix: linear lastIndexOf split; property test proves identical output to the old regex on 5,000 random inputs.

Title: Cross-tenant read: GET /inventory/recipes returns every business's recipes with ingredient cost
Repro steps:
1. Business B has a recipe using 'VICTIM-SECRET-BATTER' (₹123.45/kg)
2. Log in as inventory@ (business A)
3. GET /inventory/recipes
Expected: Only A's recipes
Actual: All recipes in the database incl. B's ingredient names and costPerUnit (where: {} on a non-scoped model).
Notes: Found by review sub-agent, reproduced. Fix: filter via menuItem.businessId.

Title: Foreign-ID link: menu items/categories accept another business's categoryId / parentId
Repro steps:
1. PATCH /menu/items/<own item> {categoryId: <B's category>}
2. Or POST /menu/categories {parentId: <B's category>}
Expected: 400 Unknown category
Actual: 200/201 — A's rows point at B's category; B's category name leaks into A's reports and B can no longer delete it (FK).
Notes: Fix: assertOwnCategory via scoped client; also rejects self-parent.

Title: Foreign-ID link: staff create/update accept a shiftId from another outlet or business
Repro steps: PATCH /staff/<own cashier> {shiftId: <B's shift>}
Expected: 400 Unknown shift
Actual: 200 — /auth/me then returns B's shift; lateness computed against it.
Notes: Fix: shift must belong to one of the caller's outlets.

Title: Manual attendance at outlet A overwrites the same staff member's clock-in record at outlet B
Repro steps:
1. Cashier works at outlets A and B, clocked in at B on D
2. Manager of A only: POST /attendance/manual {userId, date: D, status: ABSENT}
Expected: A gets its own ABSENT record; B's PRESENT record untouched
Actual: B's record changed to ABSENT (lookup by userId+date only) — payroll impact.
Notes: Fix: existing-record lookup includes outletId.

Title: Leave approval skips the rank chain: a manager can approve a peer manager's leave
Repro steps: Manager X: PATCH /attendance/leaves/<Manager Y's leave> {status: APPROVED}
Actual: 200 APPROVED
Notes: Fix: canManageAttendanceOf, same rule as manual attendance.

Title: Editing a staff member's outlets as a manager silently removes their assignments at outlets the manager doesn't manage
Repro steps: Cashier in outlets A+B; manager of A: PATCH /staff/<cashier> {outletIds:[A]}
Expected: Cashier still in A and B
Actual: Cashier removed from B (deleteMany: {})
Notes: Fix: non-owners replace only assignments within their own outlets.

Title: Socket.io outlet room broadcasts every event to every role — delivery partners (and kitchen/inventory) receive other customers' phone + address
Repro steps:
1. Connect a socket as delivery@ with outletId
2. Cashier creates a COD delivery order (not assigned to this partner)
3. Observe events
Expected: Partner receives only own deliveries (README 'Who sees what')
Actual: Partner receives kot:new, order:created, order:paid and delivery:updated (713 bytes incl. customer phone 9123456780 and address) for an unassigned order.
Notes: Design proposal: per-permission rooms (outlet:<id>:ops for delivery:manage/kot:view…; partners only in user:<id>, delivery events for them via emitToUser). Touches ~55 emit sites → asking before implementing.

Title: Fire-and-forget promises without .catch can crash the API process (Node exits on unhandled rejection)
Repro steps:
1. DB blip while a reservation job notifies, a webhook alert runs, or a partner cash alert runs
2. notify()/runForOutlet()/cashBalance() rejects
Expected: Error logged; API keeps serving
Actual: Unhandled rejection → process terminates (no unhandledRejection handler) → outage for all tenants.
Notes: 4 sites: jobs-service.ts:67,90; public.ts:79; delivery.ts:768. Fix: .catch + process-level unhandledRejection logger.

Repro steps: NODE_ENV=production without MSG91 keys; POST /auth/otp/request
Expected: No OTP in logs
Actual: '[sms:dev] OTP for 98765…: 482913' logged

Title: Menu import: Excel error cells (#N/A, #REF!) and error formula results are imported as the text "[object Object]"
Repro steps: Upload a sheet whose Name/Price cell is =VLOOKUP(...) returning #N/A
Expected: Cell treated as blank → row error

Title: Bill total depends on the order items were added: allocation ties broken by array position move a paisa between lines with different tax rates
Repro steps: computeBill([A 5%, B 0%]) vs computeBill([B, A]) with 10% service charge + ₹34.04 packaging (fast-check counterexample)
Expected: Identical totals for any line order (brief: order-independent)
Actual: ₹16,553.95 vs ₹16,553.94 (1 paisa tax difference); after round-off can become ₹1 when the pre-round total sits on a 50-paise boundary.
Notes: Fix: largest-remainder ties broken by weight, then a canonical line key (rates, price, qty, discount) — never by position.

Title: A bigger discount can raise the bill: fixed extra charges (packaging/delivery) are taxed at the rates of the lines they're allocated to, and near-100% discounts shift them onto a higher-rate line
Repro steps: ₹1.00 item with 14.5% VAT (₹0.41 line discount) + 13 × ₹0.02 at 0%, ₹16.86 packaging; FLAT ₹0.03 vs ₹0.76 bill discount
Expected: Monotonic: more discount never costs more
Actual: ₹0.76 discount bill is higher than the ₹0.03 one (bounded by charges × rate spread)
Notes: GST treats such charges as part of a composite supply taxed at the PRINCIPAL supply's rate, not proportionally. Proposal for Phase 14: tax extra charges at the rate of the highest-value line. Changes documented behaviour → needs approval.

Title: Invoice numbering overflows Rule 46's 16-character limit: with a 5-char prefix the 100,000th bill of a FY throws inside the order transaction and billing stops for the outlet
Repro steps: Outlet invoicePrefix 'ABCDE' (allowed by schema); 100,000th bill in a FY → formatInvoiceNumber('ABCDE', 2026, 100000)
Expected: Numbering always fits 16 chars for any allowed prefix
Actual: Throws 'exceeds the 16-character GST limit' → order creation fails (≈ day 333 of the FY at 300 bills/day).
Notes: Options: (a) max prefix 4 chars (then 6-digit seq fits); (b) 2-digit FY 'INV/26/000001'; (c) per-FY 'YY-YY' series. Changes the documented INV-2026-00234 format → asking.

Title: Thermal receipt lines exceed the paper width for long unbroken item names and long cashier/customer/table names
Repro steps: Item 'Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious-Paneer-Butter-Masala' on 58 mm
Expected: Every line ≤ 32 chars (58 mm) / 48 (80 mm)
Actual: 55-char line → printer wraps mid-line, columns misaligned
Notes: Fix: hard-wrap over-long words; wrap Cashier/Customer/Table lines.

Title: Money fields have no upper bound in validation, but DB columns are int4 (max ₹2.14 crore) → out-of-range prices/totals fail inside Postgres as 500
Repro steps: POST /menu/items {price: 2147483648}
Expected: 400 validation error
Actual: Passes zod; Postgres int4 overflow → 500
Notes: Proposal: paise schema max 2,147,483,647 and a business cap on unit price (e.g. ₹10 lakh) — cap value needs approval.

Title: Client-supplied createdAt is accepted on any bill without bounds: drives invoice FY, coupon/happy-hour time, item time slots and the report date → backdating into closed FYs, future-dated bills, expired coupons
Repro steps: Cashier: POST /orders {orderType: TAKEAWAY, createdAt: '2024-06-01T06:00:00Z', items:[…]}
Expected: 400 outside the allowed offline window
Actual: 201, invoice INV-2024-xxxxx in FY 2024-25, createdAt 2024-06-01
Status: Deferred — needs the allowed offline window
Notes: Proposal: accept createdAt only via /orders/sync, ≤ 5 min in the future, ≤ N hours old (N = 72?) and never in a closed FY; evaluate coupons at server time for stale bills.

Title: UPI QR pays a placeholder handle: without Razorpay and without an outlet UPI ID the QR's payee is the hard-coded 'canavo@upi' (production too)
Repro steps: Outlet with no UPI ID, Razorpay not configured; POST /orders/:id/upi-qr
Expected: Refuse: 'Set the outlet's UPI ID'
Actual: QR with upi://pay?pa=canavo@upi&am=… — customer's money goes to whoever owns that handle
Notes: Fix: no placeholder payee; also the old pending QR is now failed only after the new QR is created (orders + delivery).

Repro steps: WATI configured; network down; POST /orders/:id/share/whatsapp
Expected: Fallback wa.me link
